extracted.intended_audience: young/adolescent aspiring writers and teachers (readers of Stone Soup)
extracted.subtask_description: A short, interview-based advice page collecting Rick Riordan's tips and related resources aimed at young or beginning writers, especially those interested in myth-based children's and YA fiction. Includes practical habits, stylistic guidance, and reading/research recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read a lot.
rubrics_metrics.description: Reading is one of the best preparations for writing. (Listed as Riordan's top tip: 'Read a lot.')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expose yourself to many authors, series, and reference works; use reading to learn voice, structure, pacing, and genre expectations. The page emphasizes following authors' blogs and interviews online as additional reading of authorial practice and commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice — write every day.
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice. You have to write every day. (Riordan's top tip encouraging daily writing practice.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop a daily writing habit to build skill and discipline. The item is presented as nondiscretionary advice for young writers to improve craft through repetition.

rubrics_metrics.name: You can't give up.
rubrics_metrics.description: You can’t give up. (Riordan's top tip advocating persistence.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat perseverance as a core requirement of the writing life: keep submitting, revising, and learning even in the face of rejection or slow progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Find the story that you are meant to tell.
rubrics_metrics.description: ‘Find the story that you are meant to tell.’ (Riordan advises writers to locate the story that feels most true to them.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize projects that reflect your own voice, interests, and obsessions rather than writing to trends or markets. This helps produce more authentic, sustained work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use humor to tell a story, communicate with readers, and break the darkness of difficult stories.
rubrics_metrics.description: Using humor to tell a story, communicate with readers, and break the darkness of difficult stories. (Referenced in an interview noting Riordan's use of humor and 'snarkiness' for middle-school perspective.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ humor strategically to balance tone, create voice appropriate to young protagonists, and maintain reader engagement when dealing with heavy themes. Examples given: Riordan's Percy Jackson voice and interviews discussing humor and snarkiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leave room for the reader’s imagination; make space for the reader to inhabit the story; beware epilogues.
rubrics_metrics.description: Riordan talks about leaving room for the reader’s imagination — making space for the reader to inhabit the story, and the danger of epilogues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer implication and showing over over-explanation. Avoid closing every question with lengthy epilogues that can limit readers' imaginative participation; allow readers to fill in some details themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research and read source material (myths) to inform writing.
rubrics_metrics.description: If you want to get deeper into the Greek myths, then we recommend the following books. (The page lists recommended myth retellings and reference works.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do background reading in the relevant mythic or cultural source material to enrich worldbuilding, accuracy, and inspiration. The page recommends D’Aulaires’ volumes, Roger Lancelyn Green retellings, Robert Graves, Edith Hamilton, Bulfinch, and other classics as starting points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with living authors via blogs, Twitter, websites and interviews for learning and inspiration.
rubrics_metrics.description: We are fortunate that through the internet it is possible to keep in touch with living authors through their blogs, twitter feeds, and their websites. Many authors have also posted interviews on the internet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow authors’ social media and read/watch their interviews to learn craft insights, career advice, and creative inspiration. The page links to Riordan’s website, blog, Twitter, Facebook, and many interviews as resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use companion guides and supplementary materials to enrich series worldbuilding.
rubrics_metrics.description: There are also companion guides to the myths, produced to go with the books: The Demigod Files; Percy Jackson's Greek Gods; Brooklyn House Magician’s Manual; Hotel Valhalla Guide to the Norse Worlds, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider official companion books and guides as resources for consistent worldbuilding details, lore, and ideas for expanding a series or creating immersive elements that appeal to readers.
